source_fields.instance: Arm reward distributions are fixed, unknown, and supported on $[0,1]$, with a unique best arm. The arm count $K$, budget $T$, and bound $h$ are public, and $H(\nu)=\sum_{i\ne b}(\mu_b-\mu_i)^{-2}\le h$. Neither the actual gaps nor $H$ are revealed.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Each fixed distribution nu_i is supported on [0,1], and every call returns a fresh independent sample.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: The instance satisfies H(ν) = Σ_{i≠b}(μ_b − μ_i)⁻² ≤ h, with unique best arm b. Only the upper bound h is public; the actual gaps are hidden.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); h: $h\ge11K^2$ (the currently documented window, public).
interaction_timing: The environment fixes an admissible ν. The learner receives K, T, and h.
At each time $t=1,\ldots,T$, select an arm using past feedback and draw one fresh sample.
Recommend one arm after exactly T calls.
Performance is error-event probability. There is no cumulative-regret objective.
source_fields.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
unresolved_applicability: Instance-adaptive algorithms with unknown h have a different information specification. This setting does not imply one exact error exponent shared by all instances.

operations.query_signature: Input: $t\in[T]$, $a_t\in[K]$. The declared protocol fixes timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: Select an arm before receiving a fresh sample. After all $T$ pulls, only internal computation and recommendation remain; no confirmation samples are added. The learner may tune to public $h$, but not to hidden gaps.

operations.coupling: Select an arm before receiving a fresh sample. After all $T$ pulls, only internal computation and recommendation remain; no confirmation samples are added. The learner may tune to public $h$, but not to hidden gaps.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and any probes permitted by the specification. The environment determines current losses, outcomes, or fresh samples. The learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional oracle reveals means, gaps, optimal sampling proportions, or posteriors. Statistics, likelihood ratios, and allocation optimizations are computed internally from observed samples and the public model.

source_fields.feasibility: Recommend one arm in $[K]$. Stopping and fixed-budget rules follow the declared protocol.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.

source_fields.normalization: Retain sample count, error probability, or relative asymptotic difficulty as defined here; do not rewrite them as cumulative regret.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The best-arm-identification model requires a unique best arm. Finiteness of expected stopping time and error-exponent endpoints follow the contract's specific conditions.

components.description: Sequential arm-sampling times within the fixed budget, exactly T in total.
Use a fixed number $T$ of arm pulls and compare error probability, not expected stopping time.

source_fields.budget_semantics: Use exactly T arm pulls, then recommend one arm to minimize worst-case error probability.
source_fields.scalarization: Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
source_fields.online_cost: All causal algorithms that know $h$ are permitted. UCB-E is tuned using this public upper bound. Empirical means, index comparisons, and recommendation are internal computations. Exponential-order error comparisons retain polynomial prefactors and their validity windows.
source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All causal randomized algorithms using $K,T,h$ are allowed, with exactly $T$ samples. Hidden gaps and true $H$ are inaccessible.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed. Policies know h; UCB-E tuning uses that public complexity bound. Sample means, index comparisons, and recommendations are internal work. Error-exponent comparisons retain polynomial prefactors and validity windows; feedback complexity gives no arithmetic or bit bound.
source_fields.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.

source_fields.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
source_fields.time_uniformity: The horizon T is fixed and public. The guarantee holds for that T; it does not automatically give an anytime result or a simultaneous high-probability statement for all T.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm knows a hardness upper bound controlling all arm gaps and identifies the best arm under a fixed sample budget. Performance is the maximum identification error over that hardness class. Constants in an error exponent and multiplicative approximation of the probability are different comparisons.

Public $h$ bounds instance complexity through $H\le h$. Individual arm gaps remain hidden.
